root_cause.text: The memcg refill_stock() path in mm/memcontrol.c incorrectly called get_random_u32_below() to choose a victim slot even though memcg charge draining can run in NMI context, exposing the random subsystem’s per-CPU batched_entropy_u32 local_lock to unsafe NMI reentry and state corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “get_random_u32_below() is not safe to call in the nmi context and memcg charge draining can happen in nmi context,” and explains that it “acquires a per-cpu local_lock via local_lock_irqsave()” so “an NMI that lands on a CPU mid-update ... would corrupt that state”; the patch removes get_random_u32_below(NR_MEMCG_STOCK) from refill_stock() and replaces it with a per-CPU round-robin drain_idx guarded by the existing memcg_stock local_trylock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a per-CPU `drain_idx` state field to `memcg_stock_pcp` so drain-related logic can track an index in each stock structure.
intent_record.what: A new field `uint8_t drain_idx;` was added to the `struct memcg_stock_pcp` definition immediately after the existing `unsigned long flags;` member.
intent_record.how: This extends each per-CPU `memcg_stock_pcp` instance with one byte of state that can be used to track a drain index at runtime, enabling later code to store per-CPU drain progress or selection information in the structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace random stock draining with a wraparound round-robin index in refill_stock() to provide deterministic and fair slot eviction when no empty slot exists.
intent_record.what: The fallback slot selection in refill_stock() was changed from choosing a random index with get_random_u32_below(NR_MEMCG_STOCK) to using stock->drain_idx++ as a rotating index, with added wraparound logic that resets stock->drain_idx to 0 when it reaches NR_MEMCG_STOCK, before calling drain_stock(stock, i).
intent_record.how: When no empty slot is available, the code now drains stock entries in deterministic round-robin order instead of randomly selecting one, ensuring all slots are visited fairly over time and avoiding arbitrary eviction behavior during stock refill.

relevance_review.reason: Adding a per-CPU drain_idx to memcg_stock_pcp directly supports replacing random victim-slot selection in the memcg drain/refill path, which is the root cause of the unsafe get_random_u32_below() use in NMI context.

The change removes the random victim-slot selection in refill_stock() and replaces it with a deterministic round-robin index, directly addressing the root cause that get_random_u32_below() was unsafe when refill_stock() could run in NMI context.

candidates.rationale: This directly embodies the root cause: refill_stock() used get_random_u32_below() to pick a victim slot, but this path can execute during memcg charge draining in NMI context, making the random subsystem call unsafe due to NMI reentry on its per-CPU local_lock-protected state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement invokes the random subsystem from refill_stock() to select a victim slot. Because this path can run during memcg charge draining in NMI context, calling get_random_u32_below() can reenter the per-CPU batched entropy state protected by local_lock, causing unsafe NMI reentry and potential state corruption.
